issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee in possession may enforce an independent lease-back right to recover possession from the mortgagor.
material_facts: The mortgagee received possession of the mortgaged house under a mortgage deed.
A rent note executed at the same time required monthly rent, allowed eviction for rent default, and required the mortgagor to vacate when asked.
The rent differed from the mortgage interest, and the rent note imposed obligations beyond securing payment of interest.
The mortgagee’s successors sued for possession based on the rent note after alleging that rent had not been paid.
issues.conclusion: The rent note created rights independent of the mortgage, and the mortgagee could sue for possession under it; the ejectment claim was maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: The court gives effect to the lease terms where they create rights independent of the mortgage, even though the lease-back arose from the mortgage with possession. Under Order 34, Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the mortgagee cannot deprive the mortgagor of the right to redeem except by proceeding on the mortgage, but that does not bar a possession suit based on an enforceable lease right. The court approved Lalchand v. Nenuram and considered, among other cases, Harilal Bhagwanji v. Hemshanker, Ramnarain v. Sukhi, Umeshwar Prasad v. Dwarika Prasad, Ganpat Ruri v. Md. Asraf Ali, and Jankidas v. Laxminarain.

predicates.possession_claim_under_lease: The proceeding is a claim by a mortgagee for possession based on a lease-back to the mortgagor.
predicates.mortgagee_received_possession_under_mort: The mortgagee received possession of the property under the mortgage arrangement.
predicates.lease_back_grants_independent_tenancy_ri: The lease-back imposes tenancy obligations or grants tenancy rights independent of merely securing the mortgage debt.

issues.definition: When a mortgagee seeks possession under a lease-back that grants independent tenancy rights and received possession under the mortgage, the mortgagee may enforce the lease-based possession right.

issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee’s rights do not merge into a preliminary mortgage decree merely because the time to obtain a final decree for sale has expired.
material_facts: A preliminary decree for sale was passed in the mortgage suit.
The mortgagee’s successors did not obtain a final decree for sale within the applicable time, and their application for one was dismissed as time-barred.
The mortgaged property had not been sold, and the mortgagor continued to have the right to redeem it.
issues.conclusion: The mortgagee’s rights did not merge into the preliminary decree; the mortgagee lost the remedy of recovering the debt by sale of the property, but the mortgage security otherwise remained intact.
issues.legal_principle: A preliminary decree for sale does not merge or extinguish the mortgagee’s underlying rights. Failure to obtain a final decree within the applicable time bars recovery of the mortgage money by sale, while the security and the mortgagor’s right to redeem continue.

rule.if: mortgage_decree_enforcement_dispute and preliminary_sale_decree_entered and final_sale_application_time_barred and property_not_sold

predicates.mortgage_decree_enforcement_dispute: The proceeding concerns the effect of a preliminary mortgage decree on later enforcement rights.
predicates.preliminary_sale_decree_entered: A preliminary decree for sale was entered in the mortgage proceeding.
predicates.final_sale_application_time_barred: The mortgagee's application to obtain a final decree for sale was rejected as out of time.
predicates.property_not_sold: The mortgaged property was not sold under a final decree for sale.

issues.definition: If a preliminary sale decree has been entered, the final-decree application is out of time, and the property has not been sold, the mortgage security remains although the sale remedy is lost.

issues.legal_issue: Expiry of the time to obtain a final mortgage-sale decree does not extinguish an independent right to sue for possession under a continuing rent note.
material_facts: The rent note gave the mortgagee a right to seek possession from the mortgagor.
The rent-note right continued despite the expiry of the time to apply for a final decree for sale.
The mortgagee’s successors brought a suit for possession based on the rent note.
issues.conclusion: Section 28 of the Limitation Act, 1908 did not extinguish the mortgagee’s independent right to sue for possession under the rent note.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28 of the Limitation Act, 1908 extinguishes a right to property when the period limited for instituting a suit for possession of that property has expired. It does not extinguish a continuing, independent right to sue for possession under a rent note merely because the time to apply for a final decree for sale under the mortgage has expired.

rule.if: limitation_challenge_in_lease_possession_suit and rent_note_right_continues and rent_note_right_is_independent and final_sale_application_time_barred

predicates.limitation_challenge_in_lease_possession: The proceeding challenges a mortgagee's suit for possession under a rent note on limitation grounds.
predicates.rent_note_right_continues: The right to seek possession under the rent note remains in force.
predicates.rent_note_right_is_independent: The rent-note right to possession is independent of the mortgage remedy to obtain a sale of the property.
predicates.final_sale_application_time_barred: The time to apply for a final decree for sale under the mortgage has expired.

issues.definition: Where a continuing independent rent-note right is enforced in a possession suit, expiry of the time to obtain a final mortgage-sale decree does not extinguish that right.
